RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Rowan Ellison
Member ID: W486282210
Reference/Tracking Number: POC-5D5B151DE3-65694
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-17
Requested Service/CPT: ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888
Treating Surgeon: Dr. Okafor, MD, Orthopedic Surgery [contact information not provided in records]

To the Appeals and Grievances Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for arthroscopic ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888), as stated in your Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-17. This appeal is timely, as it is being submitted well within the 180-day window identified in that notice (deadline 2027-02-13).

**Stated reason for denial**
Your notice states that the request was denied because "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery."

**Basis for this appeal**

Ambetter of North Carolina delegates utilization management of non-emergent knee surgery, including CPT 29888, to Evolent (formerly National Imaging Associates, "NIA"). Evolent's Knee Arthroscopy clinical guideline — referenced in Evolent's public Clinical Tip Sheet as "Guideline Evolent_CG-316," the predecessor numbering to the currently effective version I am aware is designated Evolent_CG_1764 — sets out the criteria that should have been applied to this request. I have not been able to independently retrieve the full current-version text of Evolent_CG_1764 beyond its table of contents and general-requirements section, so where I quote below, I am quoting language retrieved directly from Evolent's published Knee Arthroscopy guideline documents (the general-requirements section, which I confirmed appears in both the predecessor and current version of the guideline) and from Evolent's Knee Arthroscopy Clinical Tip Sheet (dated 02/28/2024), which explicitly summarizes the ACL-specific criteria under that same guideline. I ask that the plan confirm that the ACL-specific criteria in the currently effective version, Evolent_CG_1764, are unchanged from what is quoted below, and provide me with a copy of that section if it differs.

1. **The guideline's own ACL-specific pathway does not require a conservative-treatment trial where instability and MRI findings are present.**

The Evolent Knee Arthroscopy guideline, as summarized in the Clinical Tip Sheet, states:

"ACL reconstruction requests do not require non-operative treatment provided the following criteria are met: Knee instability (as defined subjectively as 'giving way', 'giving out', 'buckling', two-fist sign) with clinical findings of instability: Lachman's 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B, 3A, 3B, Anterior Drawer, Pivot Shift test, or instrumented (KT-1000 or KT-2000) laxity of greater than 3 mm side-side difference; MRI results confirm complete ACL tear; Member has no evidence of severe arthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) on weight-bearing x-rays; OR At least ONE of the following criteria are met: MRI results confirm ACL tear associated with other ligamentous instability or repairable meniscus; Acute ACL tear confirmed by MRI in high demand occupation or competitive athlete (any level of participation); Member has no evidence of severe arthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) on weightbearing x-rays."

The clinical record submitted with the prior authorization request satisfies this pathway:

- Subjective instability: The record documents recurrent instability with pivoting and two episodes of the knee giving way on stairs — directly matching the guideline's example of "giving way" as a qualifying subjective instability finding.
- Clinical findings of instability: Exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected side. [The specific named test (e.g., Lachman, anterior drawer, pivot shift) and grade, or KT-1000/2000 measurement, are not specified in the excerpt of records provided to me; I ask that Dr. Okafor's office supply that detail directly to the reviewer if it is not already in the chart.]
- MRI-confirmed complete tear: The MRI dated 2026-07-01 documents a "complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with bone bruise pattern."
- No severe arthritis: The same MRI documents menisci intact and no significant arthritis. [The specific Kellgren-Lawrence grade on weight-bearing x-ray, if obtained, is not stated in the records provided; if a weight-bearing x-ray was performed, I ask that it be added to the file, as the guideline specifies this grading is based on weight-bearing radiographs rather than MRI.]

Because the guideline's own ACL-specific criteria state that non-operative treatment is not a precondition to medical necessity once these findings are present, the stated denial reason — absence of an adequate conservative-treatment trial — does not appear to be a basis for denial under the plan's own applicable criteria for ACL reconstruction.

2. **Even if a conservative-treatment trial were required, the record independently documents one that meets the guideline's general non-operative management framework.**

The general requirements section of Evolent's Knee Arthroscopy guideline states that, unless otherwise specified for a particular procedure, "non-operative management must include at least TWO or more of the following, unless otherwise specified: Rest or activity modifications/limitations; Ice/heat; Protected weight bearing; Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol; Brace/orthosis; Physical therapy modalities; Supervised home exercise; Weight optimization; Injections: corticosteroid, NSAID, viscosupplementation."

The record shows all of the following completed prior to the request:

- Physical therapy modalities: Supervised physical therapy for range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, 14 weeks (2026-03-27 to 2026-07-03), 20 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- Brace/orthosis: Bracing during the same period.
- Pharmacologic treatment: NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- Injection: Corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-28, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.

This is four of the nine listed modalities — twice the "at least TWO" threshold stated in the guideline — sustained over 14 months of progressive symptoms. To the extent the denial was based on a belief that no conservative trial was attempted or documented, that belief is contradicted by the physical therapy discharge note, medication history, and injection record already in the prior authorization packet.

3. **General requirements for elective knee arthroscopy are also met.**

The guideline's general requirements section states that elective arthroscopic knee surgery "may be considered if the following general criteria are met," including "clinical correlation of the individual's subjective complaints with objective exam findings and/or imaging" and that "[the] individual does not have an active local or systemic infection" and "does not have active, untreated drug dependency." The record confirms no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoking status, and the subjective complaint of instability is corroborated by both MRI findings (complete ACL tear, bone bruise) and physical examination (positive provocative testing, limited range of motion).

**Requested action**

Based on the foregoing, I request that Ambetter of North Carolina reverse the denial of CPT 29888 and approve the requested ACL reconstruction. In the alternative, I request:

1. A copy of the complete, currently effective version of the guideline actually applied to this determination (including guideline number and effective date), so that the specific criterion said not to be met can be identified with precision; and
2. An opportunity for Dr. Okafor to participate in a peer-to-peer review with the reviewing clinician.

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to the address and phone number above. I can be reached at [phone number] and [email address] if additional information is needed.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Rowan Ellison
Member ID: W486282210
